name: Abbeville Opera House
unique: A 1908 opera house on the town square that still runs plays, concerts and film nights under a painted ceiling, with a balcony that has not lost its small town hush.
buzz: People are surprised by the quality for a town this size, and the staff let you look around after the show. Check the season calendar before driving in.

name: Abbeville Historic District
unique: A courthouse square that claims to be the birthplace of the secession movement, ringed by 19th century storefronts, a Confederate monument and a granite marker where the first secession meeting was held in 1860.
buzz: It is a quiet, handsome square rather than a museum, and the self guided plaque walk takes an hour. Pair it with the opera house and lunch on the square.

name: Abbeville County Museum
unique: A county museum run by the historical society with farm tools, cotton ledgers, old photographs and the kind of local detail no state museum bothers with.
buzz: Small and volunteer run, so call before you go. People who stop say the genealogy files are the real draw.

name: Aiken Training Track
unique: A working thoroughbred training track where you can watch young horses gallop at dawn from the rail, on a track that has prepared winners for decades.
buzz: Go before eight and stay quiet; trainers are working, not performing. Photographers love the fog and the light, and there is no admission.

name: Hitchcock Woods
unique: One of the largest urban forests in the country, 2,100 acres of longleaf pine and sand roads in the middle of Aiken, where horses and pedestrians share the trails.
buzz: Locals use it daily and visitors are welcome on foot. The sand is soft, the shade is real, and the loop to the bridge makes an easy two hours.

name: Aiken Polo Club Sunday Polo
unique: Sunday polo on grass at one of the oldest clubs in the country, where you park on the rail, bring a chair and watch four chukkers with a drink.
buzz: Cheap, relaxed and genuinely social. People bring picnics and dogs, and first timers are told to walk the field at halftime to stomp divots.

name: Hopelands Gardens
unique: A free 14 acre garden of live oaks, camellias and reflecting pools behind the old Hope estate, with a thoroughbred stable that is now an events hall.
buzz: Quiet, shaded and free, which makes it the default picnic spot in town. The Christmas lights in December are a local tradition.

name: Bamberg County Museum
unique: A county museum in a small railroad town with Native American artifacts, cotton economy records and photographs of the Bamberg that the highway bypassed.
buzz: Volunteer run and old fashioned, in the good way. Call before driving over; hours are short.

name: Edisto River Paddle
unique: A slow blackwater river through cypress and sandbars, with rope swings, kingfishers and water the color of strong tea.
buzz: The current does most of the work, so it suits beginners. Bring a dry bag and bug spray, and check the gauge before a summer trip.

name: God's Acre Healing Springs
unique: A roadside spring on land deeded to God, where people fill jugs from four pipes for free and the water is said to have healed soldiers since the Revolution.
buzz: People drive out with a trunk full of containers. Nobody agrees on the science, but the ritual and the cold water are real, and the little church across the road is worth a look.

name: Barnwell State Park
unique: A CCC built park with a spring fed lake, a sand beach, picnic shelters and a trail through pine woods, the kind of place that has not been redesigned since the Depression.
buzz: The swimming area is shallow and good for kids, and the cabins are basic but cheap. Locals treat it as their summer backyard.

name: Mepkin Abbey
unique: A Trappist monastery on the Cooper River with formal gardens, a church by Clare Boothe Luce and a small cemetery, where monks still keep the hours of prayer.
buzz: Visitors are asked to respect the silence and dress modestly. The gardens and the river walk are the draw, and the gift shop sells mushrooms grown on the abbey farm.

name: Old Santee Canal Park
unique: The remains of America's first true canal, opened in 1800, with a museum, a boardwalk over the swamp and a replica canal boat.
buzz: The interpretive center explains why the canal failed, which is more interesting than it sounds. Alligators are common in the swamp, so keep small kids close.

name: Cypress Gardens
unique: A cypress swamp garden dug by hand in the 1930s, with a flat bottom boat that poles you through trees draped in Spanish moss and water black as ink.
buzz: The boat ride is short but memorable, and the butterfly house is a hit with kids. Go early for still water and fewer people.

name: Hell Hole Swamp Festival
unique: A small town festival named for the swamp where bootleggers once ran liquor, with a parade, gospel singing, a snake show and the kind of food stalls that only exist one weekend a year.
buzz: It is deliberately unpolished and that is the appeal. Parking is in fields, bring cash, and stay for the gospel program.

name: Calhoun County Museum
unique: A county collection with farm implements, a one room school exhibit and records from the cotton and phosphate days, kept going by people who grew up with the objects.
buzz: Friendly and small. Ask about the phosphate history; the county was a world supplier before the industry moved.

name: Congaree Bluffs Heritage Preserve
unique: A high bluff over the Congaree River floodplain, with a steep trail down to sandbars and a view across a forest that floods every spring.
buzz: The trail is short and steep, and the bluff edge is unfenced, so watch kids. Birders come for the migration and the river bottom hardwoods.

name: Chester State Park
unique: A CCC park around a 160 acre lake, with stone picnic shelters, a swimming beach and a trail that circles the water through oak and pine.
buzz: Quiet even in summer, and the cabins are a bargain. The lake is more for paddling and fishing than swimming.

name: Chester County Museum
unique: A small museum in a railroad town with Catawba pottery, cotton mill artifacts and photographs of the textile strike that shaped the county.
buzz: Volunteers will talk your ear off if you ask about the mills. Call first, because hours are volunteer dependent.

name: Cheraw State Park
unique: A CCC park with a cypress lined lake, a boardwalk, a swimming beach and a golf course cut through the sandhills, all built by the Civilian Conservation Corps.
buzz: The lake trail is easy and pretty, and the golf course is one of the best value rounds in the state. Cabins book far ahead.

name: Carolina Sandhills National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Forty five thousand acres of longleaf pine and sandhill scrub managed for the red cockaded woodpecker, with a driving loop, trails and a wiregrass understory that blooms after fire.
buzz: The woodpeckers are the prize and the staff will tell you which clusters are active. Bring water, ticks are real, and the auto tour is the easiest way in.

name: Cheraw Historic District
unique: A river town of antebellum houses, a 19th century market hall and a theater where jazz bands played on the chitlin circuit, all within a few blocks.
buzz: Pick up a walking tour map at the chamber and look for the Dizzy Gillespie marker; he was born here. The town is quiet, so the architecture is the show.

name: Santee National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Fifteen thousand acres of Lake Marion bottomland where thousands of ducks, geese and eagles winter, with a boardwalk, a driving route and a small visitor center.
buzz: Winter is the season. The Cuddo unit loop is the reliable drive, and alligators are common in warm months, so keep dogs leashed.

name: Clarendon County Museum
unique: A county museum with farm life exhibits, Native American pieces and the local story of the school desegregation case that preceded Brown v. Board.
buzz: The Briggs v. Board story is the reason to go, and the volunteers tell it well. Hours are limited, so call.

name: Cypress Wetlands
unique: A boardwalk loop through a cypress swamp in the middle of town, with nesting herons, egrets and ibis a few feet from the rail.
buzz: Free, flat and easy, and the birds are ridiculously close. Go in spring for chicks, and bring binoculars rather than a flash.

name: Edisto Beach State Park
unique: A beach park with maritime forest trails, a boneyard beach of fallen trees and a campground under live oaks, plus an environmental learning center.
buzz: The beach is quieter than the resort islands and the forest trail is a real hike. Loggerhead turtles nest in summer, and the rangers run night walks.

name: ACE Basin
unique: One of the largest undeveloped estuaries on the Atlantic coast, where the Ashepoo, Combahee and Edisto rivers braid through marsh and cypress, and dolphins and eagles are routine.
buzz: Launch at Bennett's Point or Edisto and follow the marked paddling trail. There is no visitor center at the heart of it, which is why it stays quiet.

name: Darlington Raceway
unique: The track they call Too Tough to Tame, a one and a quarter mile oval with an egg shaped turn forced by a minnow pond the builders would not move.
buzz: Even casual fans leave hoarse. The spring Cup race is the big one, and the museum and track tour run on non race days.

name: Kalmia Gardens
unique: A thirty acre garden on a bluff over Black Creek, with mountain laurel, camellias and a boardwalk down to a blackwater swamp in the middle of a small city.
buzz: Free and rarely crowded, with a steep boardwalk that is worth the climb back. Spring azaleas are the peak.

name: Darlington County Museum
unique: A county archive and museum in a 19th century house, with racing memorabilia, cotton records and family files that go back to the first settlers.
buzz: The racing corner is the fun part, and the staff pull files for genealogy visitors. Call before you go.

name: Dillon Motor Speedway
unique: A short asphalt oval on the NASCAR weekly circuit where late models and street stocks run under the lights, and a grandstand ticket costs less than a movie.
buzz: Loud, cheap and friendly. The concession stand is a church group, and kids run the hill behind the stands during cautions.

name: Little Pee Dee State Park
unique: A quiet park on a cypress lake beside the Little Pee Dee River, with a nature trail, a fishing pier and campsites under pines.
buzz: It is a locals' park with no crowds. The trail is short, the fishing is the point, and the river swamp feel is genuine.

name: Dillon County Museum
unique: A county museum with tobacco farming tools, railroad history and the story of the county's namesake, a railroad surveyor.
buzz: Small and earnest, with volunteers who know the tobacco economy firsthand. Call for hours.

name: Colonial Dorchester State Historic Site
unique: The tabby ruins of a 1697 trading town on the Ashley River, with a brick fort, a church bell tower and oyster shell concrete walls that have lasted three centuries.
buzz: It is a ruin, not a reconstruction, and that is the appeal. The river walk and the giant live oaks make it a good picnic stop.

name: Givhans Ferry State Park
unique: A CCC park where the Edisto River bends into a sand beach and a bluff, with cabins, a ferry landing and a paddling put in.
buzz: The river is the reason. Tubing and kayaking are easy here, and the cabins overlook the water. Summer weekends fill up.

name: Flowertown Festival
unique: One of the largest arts and crafts festivals in the state, spread through azalea filled streets, with a children's carnival and food from church kitchens.
buzz: Go early for parking and expect crowds by noon. The plant sale and the local pottery are the picks.
